title.narrative: Partnering with SIDS to deliver a 75% reduction in Plastic Pollution

description.narrative: Partner countries: Grenada, St Lucia, Papua New Guinea, Guinea Bissau, Tuvalu. Regional components include the Pacific, Caribbean, and Indian Ocean regions.

Partnering with SIDS to build sustainable blue economies through reduction in plastic pollution.
This programme supports Small Island Developing States (SIDS) to reduce plastic pollution through evidence-based national policy planning, targeted implementation support and complementary regional solutions.
During 2024–2025, Common Seas supported partner countries to develop five national policy plans and recommendation reports across Grenada, Saint Lucia, Papua New Guinea, Guinea-Bissau and Tuvalu. These outputs established plastic waste baselines, modelled future pollution scenarios and identified policy pathways with the potential to reduce plastic pollution by approximately 40% to 79% over ten years.
During 2025–2026, the programme moved from policy development towards implementation readiness. This included financial assessments for Saint Lucia and Guinea-Bissau, embedded technical support to strengthen institutional capacity in both countries, and development of the Scope of Work for a regional Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) feasibility study with the Indian Ocean Commission.
During 2026–2027, the programme is supporting governments and regional partners to move from implementation planning towards delivery. In Papua New Guinea, support includes a cost-benefit analysis of priority single-use plastic measures and an indicative cost assessment for expanding waste collection services. In Tuvalu, technical support focuses on strengthening the Waste Management Levy and Container Deposit Scheme and assessing improvements to waste management infrastructure and the Funafuti dumpsite. In Saint Lucia, the programme is supporting development of reuse approaches within the hospitality sector, including stakeholder engagement, technical assessment and preparation of a Reuse Opportunity Assessment.
At regional level, Common Seas is progressing the EPR feasibility study with the Indian Ocean Commission through country baseline and readiness assessments, development of a regional harmonisation framework, stakeholder validation and preparation of final feasibility outputs. The programme is also strengthening regional implementation partnerships through structured engagement with private sector actors, regional institutions and delivery partners, including development of a shared vision and practical pathways for future collaboration and replication.
Together, these activities combine country-level technical support, regional cooperation and partnership development to help SIDS move from policy frameworks towards practical, financially sustainable and implementable solutions, supporting longer-term reductions in plastic pollution and associated environmental impacts.

Small Island Developing States (SIDS), including national government institutions, regional organisations, local delivery partners, civil society, and private sector stakeholders involved in plastic pollution reduction, waste management, circular economy solutions, and sustainable blue economy development.

The programme is delivered through a phased approach that moves from national policy development to implementation readiness and targeted implementation support.
Phase I: National policy planning and evidence generation (2024–2025) The programme supported five SIDS to establish plastic waste baselines, analyse future waste and leakage scenarios, and develop evidence-based National Action Plans and policy recommendation reports. These outputs identified priority policy interventions and quantified pathways to reduce plastic pollution, while strengthening government ownership through stakeholder engagement, consultation and policy co-development.
Implementation readiness and regional feasibility (2025–2026) The programme supported the transition from policy development towards implementation by:
completing implementation finance assessments for Saint Lucia and Guinea-Bissau, including policy costings, financing pathways and implementation sequencing; embedding national technical support in Saint Lucia and Guinea-Bissau to strengthen institutional coordination, governance arrangements, approval pathways and implementation planning; advancing regional Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) work with the Indian Ocean Commission through stakeholder engagement and completion of the Scope of Work for a regional feasibility study; and supporting national and regional dissemination and peer learning, including the Tuvalu National Action Plan launch and Pacific SIDS peer exchange.
Implementation support and regional collaboration (2026–2027) From April 2026 to March 2027, the programme is building on these foundations through three objectives:
Strengthen national capacity and systems to deliver National Action Plans. Targeted implementation support is being delivered in Papua New Guinea, Tuvalu and Saint Lucia. In Papua New Guinea, this includes a cost-benefit analysis of priority single-use plastic measures and an indicative cost assessment for expanding waste collection services. In Tuvalu, support focuses on strengthening the Waste Management Levy and Container Deposit Scheme and assessing improvements to waste management infrastructure and the Funafuti dumpsite. In Saint Lucia, the programme is assessing opportunities to advance reuse within the hospitality sector through stakeholder engagement, technical assessment and development of a Reuse Opportunity Assessment. Advance feasible, scalable and financially sustainable solutions for SIDS. The programme is progressing the Regional EPR Feasibility Study with the Indian Ocean Commission through country baseline and readiness assessments, development of a regional harmonisation framework, stakeholder validation and preparation of final feasibility outputs. It is also identifying and progressing matchfunding opportunities to support subsequent stages of regional delivery. Strengthen regional collaboration, implementation pathways and replication. The programme is engaging private sector actors, regional institutions and delivery partners to identify practical implementation barriers and opportunities for SIDS, develop a shared regional vision and stakeholder map, test opportunities for collaboration through regional dialogue, and establish pathways for future partnership, replication and investment.
This phased approach enables partner countries and regional organisations to progress according to government priorities, implementation readiness and available financing, while linking national technical support with regional solutions and longer-term delivery partnerships.
